evidence.note: Two SetTodoList calls — an explicit running checklist created early and refreshed mid-build, indicating maintained (not merely mental) tracking of subsystems.

Enumerates a coherent list of pending fixes spanning multiple subsystems (delete markers, presigned expiry, versioned cleanup, partNumber guard, auth guards, bucket-name validation, console routing, If-None-Match), showing roughly accurate done-vs-remaining picture across areas.

Prose repeatedly names remaining work items ('remaining get_bucket_object_data_path calls', 'Now I need to fix copy_object, complete_multipart, and lifecycle worker paths'), sequencing area-by-area closure.
complete_multipart and copy_object are re-touched across many separated steps without explicit recognition of partial/incomplete state — some re-visiting rather than granular per-operation status.

Trajectory ends still working on console access-keys with no final coverage sweep against the spec's enumerated surface (error codes, notification events, all testids), so no full-horizon cross-check is demonstrated.

reasoning: The agent keeps a genuine running checklist (two todo lists) and tracks remaining work area-by-area, including a granular enumerated batch of pending fixes at step 77 — matching the level-5 anchor of 'a running checklist marked off with a roughly accurate done-vs-remaining view.' It falls short of level 8 because there is no visible recognition that subsystems are only partially done, no explicit detection of circular/thrashing debugging (multipart and copy are re-touched repeatedly), and no cross-check of the completed set against the spec's full enumerated surface of error codes/events/testids. This places it solidly at 5.
